title: Stockings by the Mantel
description: Picture a Christmas mantel through familiar fireplace parts, hanging stockings, and their knitted details.
cardDescription: Picture a Christmas mantel through familiar fireplace parts, hanging stockings, and their knitted details.
focus: The clues describe a seasonal household scene. Object parts and their positions provide the route into the answers.
solvingTip: Look for a fireplace feature, a stocking part, or a hanging action.
words: Long knitted foot covering hung as a Christmas decoration
Shelf or structure above a fireplace
Floor-level area beneath and in front of a fireplace opening
Built opening where a household fire burns
Vertical passage carrying smoke out of a building
Curved hanger used to suspend a stocking
Traditional Christmas gift-giving figure in familiar stories
To suspend a decoration from a support
Closed front end of a stocking
Back lower part of a knitted foot covering
Finished band around a stocking’s opening
Sheep’s fiber used in some knitted stockings
To form a stocking from connected yarn loops
Decorative fabric strip tied to a Christmas stocking

answerNotes.MANTEL: Mantel is the fireplace spelling. Mantle has other meanings, including a covering or responsibility.
answerNotes.HEARTH: The hearth is at the fireplace’s base. The mantel is above it, so location distinguishes the words.
answerNotes.STOCKING: Stocking names the whole foot-and-leg covering. Toe, heel, and cuff identify smaller parts.
answerNotes.CHIMNEY: A chimney is the smoke passage. It is separate from the opening where the fire itself is seen.

title: A Gingerbread House Display
description: Explore a holiday baking display through familiar house shapes, sweets, and construction-like details.
cardDescription: Explore a holiday baking display through familiar house shapes, sweets, and construction-like details.
focus: The clues name parts represented in an edible house and the materials used to decorate it. They define words rather than supplying a recipe.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a house part, a sweet material, or a display item.
words: Spiced baked dough used for a familiar holiday model house
Building shape represented in a gingerbread display
Top covering of a model holiday house
Upright side of a gingerbread building
Entrance shape marked on a model house
Opening shape represented with icing on a gingerbread wall
Sweet mixture used to join or decorate gingerbread pieces
Sweet confection used for a model house’s decorations
Small sugar-coated jelly sweet used in holiday displays
Small baked piece that can form part of a gingerbread scene
Aromatic flavoring such as ginger or cinnamon
Dark syrup traditionally used in some gingerbread recipes
Guide showing the shapes of pieces for a model
Flat support holding a completed holiday display

answerNotes.MOLASSES: Molasses is a dark syrup from sugar processing. The clue identifies an ingredient rather than a required recipe quantity.
answerNotes.PATTERN: Pattern means a shape guide here. It differs from the finished model built using those shapes.
answerNotes.ICING: Icing can join and decorate model pieces. The clue refers to the sweet material rather than frozen water.
answerNotes.GUMDROP: A gumdrop is a small jelly confection. The word names one decorative sweet rather than a whole assortment.

title: A Christmas Sweet Counter
description: Browse familiar holiday sweets, nuts, dried fruits, and warming spice words.
cardDescription: Browse familiar holiday sweets, nuts, dried fruits, and warming spice words.
focus: The clues identify foods and flavorings by familiar forms. Several words have another everyday meaning outside a sweet-shop setting.
solvingTip: Look for a confection, a dried fruit, a spice, or a serving object.
words: Soft dense confection commonly made with sugar and dairy ingredients
Candy made by cooking sugar with butter
Hard breakable confection often containing nuts
Sweet confection often made with nuts and whipped egg white
Rich chocolate confection with a soft center
Dried grape included in many holiday sweet mixtures
Small dried grape used in baking, as in a Zante variety
Strong aromatic spice made from a dried flower bud
Aromatic seed spice grated into some festive sweets
Flavoring category including clove and nutmeg
Hard-shelled edible item used in many holiday confections
Flat serving object holding an assortment of sweets
Small enjoyable food offered at a holiday gathering
Having a sugary taste, as a confection

answerNotes.BRITTLE: Brittle names a hard breakable candy here. It is also an adjective describing something that snaps easily.
answerNotes.TRUFFLE: Truffle is a chocolate confection in this clue. The same spelling also names a valuable fungus.
answerNotes.CLOVE: The spice clove is a dried flower bud. It is different from a clove of garlic.
answerNotes.CURRANT: A Zante currant is a small dried grape. Fresh red or black currants are different fruits, so the baking context matters.

title: A Christmas Carol Gathering
description: Enjoy familiar words for seasonal singing, shared melodies, and the sounds around a carol gathering.
cardDescription: Enjoy familiar words for seasonal singing, shared melodies, and the sounds around a carol gathering.
focus: The clues use singing vocabulary and ordinary holiday words. No song lyrics or recording dates are needed.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names a musical section, a singing action, or a seasonal sound.
words: Song associated with Christmas or another celebration
Ringing instruments often heard in Christmas music
Organized singers presenting seasonal music together
Words and melody performed as one musical piece
Part of a carol carrying a section of its words
Repeated section returning between song verses
Group joining together to sing a returning section
Melody followed by the carol singers
Combination of different sung notes at the same time
To produce the musical words of a carol
To pay attention to a group’s singing
Great happiness expressed in many seasonal greetings
Calm or freedom from conflict wished for in holiday messages

answerNotes.CAROL: Carol names a celebratory song here. Christmas is a familiar setting, though the word has a broader history.
answerNotes.REFRAIN: The refrain returns within the song. It can give a gathering a familiar section to join.
answerNotes.BELLS: Bells sound by vibration after being struck. The clue uses the plural because it names more than one instrument.
answerNotes.TUNE: Tune is the melody in this clue. It is a noun rather than the action of adjusting an instrument.

title: The Christmas Toy Window
description: Remember a shop window of classic toys through familiar objects, shapes, and gift details.
cardDescription: Remember a shop window of classic toys through familiar objects, shapes, and gift details.
focus: The clues describe traditional toys as objects in a holiday display. Shape and movement identify the items without brand names.
solvingTip: Look for something that rolls, spins, rings, or is put together.
words: Object made for play and displayed in a gift-shop window
Model of linked railway cars used as a classic toy
Small human-shaped figure in a toy display
Solid building piece used in a construction toy

answerNotes.TOP: Top is a spinning toy here. It does not mean the highest part of an object.
answerNotes.YOYO: Yo-yo is commonly written with a hyphen. The grid joins the letters into a single answer.
answerNotes.TEDDY: Teddy is a shortened name for a teddy bear. The clue asks for the toy name rather than a person’s name.
answerNotes.MARBLE: Marble names a small glass playing ball here. It does not refer to the decorative building stone.
